method_card.title: Family and Describing People
method_card.content:
This lesson covers family members, physical appearance and personality adjectives. You need to master adjective agreement (gender and number) and use ser for personality and tener for physical features.

SpanishEnglish
la madremother
el padrefather
el hermano / la hermanabrother / sister
el abuelo / la abuelagrandfather / grandmother
el primo / la primacousin (m/f)
el padrastro / la madrastrastepfather / stepmother
alto/atall
bajo/ashort
simpático/anice, friendly
gracioso/afunny
trabajador(a)hardworking
perezoso/alazy
Tiene el pelo largoHe/She has long hair
Tiene los ojos verdesHe/She has green eyes

Grammar focus: Adjectives ending in -o change to -a for feminine, -os for masculine plural, -as for feminine plural. Adjectives ending in -e (e.g. inteligente) only change for plural (inteligentes).

Model: Mi madre es alta y delgada con el pelo largo y moreno. Es muy simpática y trabajadora. (My mother is tall and slim with long dark hair. She is very nice and hardworking.)
steps: Learn the key vocabulary for family members and physical descriptions
Master adjective agreement rules for gender and number
Use ser for personality and tener for hair and eyes
Practice building extended descriptions using connectives like pero and además

steps.content: Break the sentence into parts: Mi hermana = My sister, es alta = is tall.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: simpática has a feminine ending (-a). Since padre is masculine, the adjective must end in -o.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The error is simpática — it should be simpático to agree with the masculine noun padre.

method_card.title: Friendships and Relationships
method_card.content:
This lesson covers friendship vocabulary, opinion phrases, and describing what makes a good friend. Key grammar: llevarse bien/mal con (reflexive verb for getting along) and a variety of opinion phrases beyond me gusta.

SpanishEnglish
el/la mejor amigo/abest friend
la amistadfriendship
la confianzatrust
el apoyosupport
fielloyal
comprensivo/aunderstanding
honesto/ahonest
divertido/afun
llevarse bien conto get on well with
llevarse mal conto get on badly with
Creo queI think that
En mi opiniónIn my opinion
A mi modo de verIn my view

Grammar focus: Llevarse is a reflexive verb: me llevo, te llevas, se lleva, nos llevamos. Use con + person. Opinion phrases: creo que, pienso que, me parece que, a mi modo de ver.

Model: Me llevo muy bien con mi mejor amiga porque es fiel y comprensiva. Creo que la confianza es lo más importante en una amistad. (I get on very well with my best friend because she is loyal and understanding. I think trust is the most important thing in a friendship.)
steps: Learn key friendship vocabulary including la amistad, la confianza, el apoyo
Master the reflexive verb llevarse bien/mal con for describing relationships
Use varied opinion phrases beyond me gusta to access higher marks
Practice giving justified opinions with porque, ya que, dado que

method_card.title: Relationships and Marriage
method_card.content:
This lesson covers relationships, marriage vocabulary, the conditional tense (I would), and future time expressions. The conditional is a Higher-level structure essential for top marks.

SpanishEnglish
la parejacouple, partner
el novio / la noviaboyfriend / girlfriend
la bodawedding
el matrimoniomarriage
casarseto get married
divorciarseto get divorced
enamorarse deto fall in love with
soltero/asingle
casado/amarried
en el futuroin the future
algún díaone day
cuando sea mayorwhen I am older
me gustaríaI would like

Grammar focus: The conditional tense is formed by adding -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían to the infinitive. Irregular stems: tendr-, podr-, querr-, har-. The phrase si tuviera la oportunidad, me gustaría... uses the imperfect subjunctive + conditional.

Model: En el futuro, me gustaría casarme y tener dos hijos. Mi boda ideal sería en la playa. (In the future, I would like to get married and have two children. My ideal wedding would be on the beach.)
steps: Learn key vocabulary for relationships and marriage
Master the conditional tense formation: infinitive + -ía endings
Memorise the irregular conditional stems: tendr-, podr-, querr-, har-
Combine conditional with future time expressions for complex sentences

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — conditional tense is tested every year

steps.content: Me gustaría = I would like (conditional of gustar).

steps.label: Step 2

wrong.gustaba: gustaba is the imperfect (I used to like). The future context needs the conditional → gustaría.

wrong.tengo: tengo is the conjugated form (I have). After me gustaría, you need the infinitive → tener.
wrong.tendría: tendría is the conditional (I would have). After me gustaría, use the infinitive → tener.

method_card.content:
This lesson covers healthy living vocabulary, expressing obligation with modal verbs (deber, tener que, poder), and the impersonal structure se debe.

fumarto smoke
la comida rápidafast food

deber + infinitivemust / should
tener que + infinitiveto have to

Grammar focus: Three ways to express obligation: Se debe (impersonal), deber (personal), tener que (have to). After any modal verb, ALWAYS use the infinitive. Common error: *debo como → should be debo comer.

Model: Para mantenerse en forma, se debe comer una dieta equilibrada y hacer ejercicio. Debería dormir más. (To keep fit, one should eat a balanced diet and exercise. I should sleep more.)
steps: Learn key vocabulary for health, diet and exercise
Master three obligation structures: se debe, deber, tener que
Always use the infinitive after modal verbs
Practice using frequency expressions: siempre, a veces, normalmente

method_card.content:
This lesson covers food and drink vocabulary, mealtimes, expressing preferences with gustar-type verbs, and using the preterite tense to say what you ate.

Grammar focus: Gustar agrees with the thing liked: me gusta el arroz (singular) vs me gustan las patatas fritas (plural). Preterite of comer: comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comieron.

Model: Me encanta la paella. Para el desayuno como tostadas. Ayer cené pescado con patatas fritas y estaba riquísimo.
steps: Learn food and drink vocabulary across all categories

method_card.title: Drugs, Smoking and Alcohol
method_card.content:
This lesson covers unhealthy habits vocabulary, giving impersonal advice using se debe / hay que / es importante, and discussing both sides of the argument about smoking, alcohol and drugs.

SpanishEnglish

vapearto vape

hay que + infinitiveit is necessary to
es importante + infinitiveit is important to
por un lado... por otro ladoon one hand... on the other
cáncer de pulmónlung cancer

Grammar focus: Impersonal advice structures: Se debe (one should), Hay que (one must), Es importante (it is important). All followed by infinitive. Balanced arguments: por un lado... por otro lado.

Model: Fumar es muy peligroso y malo para la salud. Hay riesgo de cáncer de pulmón. Se debe evitar las drogas y no se debe fumar.
steps: Learn vocabulary for smoking, alcohol and drugs

method_card.content:
This lesson covers school subject vocabulary, giving opinions with justifications, and using comparatives and superlatives to compare subjects.

Grammar focus: Me gusta + singular subject vs me gustan + plural subject. Comparatives: más + adj + que, menos + adj + que, tan + adj + como. Irregulars: mejor (better), peor (worse). Superlative: la asignatura más + adj.

Model: Me gustan las ciencias porque son interesantes. La historia es más difícil que el español. Mi asignatura preferida es la informática porque es la más divertida.
steps: Learn all school subject names in Spanish

method_card.title: School Rules, Homework and Future Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers school rules with se debe / no se puede, homework vocabulary, and the future tense (near future + simple future) for discussing post-16 plans.

SpanishEnglish
no se debe + infinitiveyou must not
no se puede + infinitiveyou cannot
llevar el uniformeto wear the uniform
no se puede utilizar el móvilyou cannot use your mobile
los debereshomework (always plural)
voy a + infinitiveI am going to
estudiaréI will study
ir a la universidadto go to university
hacer el bachilleratoto do A-levels
ganar dineroto earn money
en el futuroin the future
cuando termine el instiwhen I finish school

Grammar focus: Near future: voy a + infinitive. Simple future: infinitive + -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án. Irregular stems: tendr-, har-, podr-, querr-. School rules: se debe / no se debe / se puede / no se puede + infinitive.

Model: En mi insti no se puede utilizar el móvil. Después del instituto voy a hacer el bachillerato. Estudiaré medicina porque quiero ser médico.
steps: Learn school rule structures: se debe, no se puede, hay que
Know that los deberes (homework) is always plural in Spanish
Master the near future: ir a + infinitive
Form the simple future tense: infinitive + endings (-é, -ás, -á...)

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Take the full infinitive: estudiar.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Add the yo future ending: -é. estudiar + é = estudiaré.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: estudiaré (I will study).

Grammar focus: Use polite forms: quisiera (I would like — imperfect subjunctive of querer) or me gustaria (conditional). Use usted form with waiters: ¿Tiene...?, ¿Puede traer...?.

method_card.title: Spanish Festivals and Celebrations
method_card.content:
This lesson covers four major festivals: Las Fallas, La Tomatina, Semana Santa and El Dia de los Muertos, plus the conditional tense and festival sentence builders.

SpanishEnglish
la fiestathe festival
las fallasthe Fallas sculptures
los fuegos artificialesfireworks
un desfilea parade
tirar tomatesto throw tomatoes
divertirseto enjoy oneself
una procesiona procession
el Dia de los MuertosDay of the Dead
una ofrendaan altar/offering
me gustaria ir aI would like to go to
seria inolvidableit would be unforgettable
la fiesta tiene lugar enthe festival takes place in
durante la fiesta se puededuring the festival you can

Grammar focus: The conditional tense (seria, me gustaria, iria, encontraria) is used to say what you would do. Form it with the infinitive + endings: -ia, -ias, -ia, -iamos, -iais, -ian. Use it alongside present and preterite for a three-tense answer.

Model: Siempre he querido ir a La Tomatina ya que seria inolvidable. Durante la fiesta se puede tirar tomates y divertirse. (I have always wanted to go to La Tomatina since it would be unforgettable. During the festival you can throw tomatoes and enjoy yourself.)
steps: Learn the key facts about Las Fallas, La Tomatina, Semana Santa and El Dia de los Muertos
Master festival sentence builders: la fiesta tiene lugar en, durante la fiesta se puede
Practise using the conditional tense for hypothetical situations
Combine three tenses in your answers about festivals

steps.label: Step 2

method_card.title: Customs and Traditions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers daily life differences between Spain and the UK, family customs, Latin American traditions, and comparison structures.

SpanishEnglish
el desayunobreakfast
la comidalunch (main meal)
la cenadinner
la meriendaafternoon snack
la siestaafternoon nap/rest
dos besostwo kisses (greeting)
el paseoevening walk/stroll
la sobremesaafter-meal chat
la quinceanera15th birthday celebration
a diferencia deunlike
mientras quewhile/whereas
sin embargohowever
las costumbrescustoms

Grammar focus: Comparison structures: En Espana se come mas tarde que en Inglaterra (In Spain they eat later than in England). Use a diferencia de (unlike), mientras que (while/whereas), and sin embargo (however) for comparing cultures.

Model: En Espana la comida principal es el almuerzo, mientras que en Inglaterra es la cena. A diferencia de los britanicos, los espanoles suelen saludar con dos besos. (In Spain the main meal is lunch, whereas in England it is dinner. Unlike the British, Spaniards usually greet with two kisses.)
steps: Learn the key differences in daily life between Spain and the UK
Master comparison structures: a diferencia de, mientras que, sin embargo
Know specific customs like la siesta, el paseo, la sobremesa and la quinceanera
Practise writing structured comparisons using contrast connectives

method_card.title: Celebrity Culture and Role Models
method_card.content:
This lesson covers physical descriptions, personality adjectives, how to argue whether someone is a good or bad role model, and the imperfect tense for describing the past.

SpanishEnglish
un modelo a seguira role model
alto/atall
delgado/aslim
el pelo largolong hair
generoso/agenerous
humildehumble
trabajador/ahardworking
egoistaselfish
arrogantearrogant
tiene buenos valoreshas good values
dona dinero a buenas causasdonates money to good causes
promueve una imagen irrealpromotes an unrealistic image
era / tenia / haciaused to be / used to have / used to do

Grammar focus: The imperfect tense describes what someone used to be like or used to do: era (was/used to be), tenia (had/used to have), hacia (did/used to do), iba (went/used to go). Use alongside present and preterite for three tenses.

Model: Pienso que Rosalia es un buen modelo a seguir dado que es una cantante con mucho talento. Cuando era joven, estudiaba musica en Barcelona. (I think Rosalia is a good role model given that she is a very talented singer. When she was young, she studied music in Barcelona.)
steps: Learn physical description and personality adjective vocabulary
Master arguments for and against celebrity role models
Practise using the imperfect tense for describing the past
Build extended answers using three tenses and connectives like dado que, ya que

method_card.content:
Key Vocabulary

SpanishEnglish
las vacacionesthe holidays
ir de vacacionesto go on holiday
viajarto travel

las montañasthe mountains
el campothe countryside

el año pasadolast year

Grammar Focus — Preterite and Conditional

Use the preterite for completed past actions: fui (I went), viajé (I travelled), nadé (I swam). The preterite of ir is irregular: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. Use the conditional to say what you would do: take the infinitive and add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. Irregular stems: tener → tendr-, hacer → har-, poder → podr-.

Model Paragraph

"El verano pasado fui de vacaciones al campo con mi familia. Nadé en el río y monté en bici. Me lo pasé muy bien. El año que viene me gustaría ir a Grecia porque sería emocionante."
(Last summer I went on holiday to the countryside with my family. I swam in the river and rode a bike. I had a great time. Next year I would like to go to Greece because it would be exciting.)
steps: Learn the key holiday vocabulary and time phrases
Master the preterite tense of ir and regular -ar verbs
Practise forming the conditional with -ía endings
Build paragraphs that combine past, present, and conditional tenses

Key Vocabulary

SpanishEnglish

Grammar Focus — Imperfect for Descriptions

Use the preterite for the action of staying (me alojé — I stayed) and the imperfect for descriptions of what it was like (era grande — it was big, tenía piscina — it had a pool). Use quisiera (I would like) for polite requests in role-plays.

Model Paragraph

"Me alojé en un hotel de lujo cerca de la playa. La habitación era grande y tenía vistas al mar. Me gustó mucho porque era muy cómodo."
(I stayed in a luxury hotel near the beach. The room was big and had sea views. I liked it a lot because it was very comfortable.)

Practise combining preterite and imperfect for past accommodation

steps.label: Step 2

method_card.content:
Key Vocabulary

SpanishEnglish
en cocheby car
en trenby train
en aviónby plane
en autobúsby bus
en barcoby boat
en biciby bike
a pieon foot
siga todo rectogo straight on
tuerza a la derechaturn right
tuerza a la izquierdaturn left
cerca denear
enfrente deopposite
al lado denext to

Grammar Focus — Comparatives

Use más ... que (more ... than), menos ... que (less ... than), and tan ... como (as ... as) to compare transport. Key adjectives: rápido (fast), lento (slow), caro (expensive), barato (cheap), cómodo (comfortable). Use mejor que (better than) and peor que (worse than) for irregular comparatives.

Model Paragraph

"Prefiero viajar en tren porque es más rápido que el autobús y más cómodo que el coche. Ir en bici es mejor para el medio ambiente."
(I prefer to travel by train because it is faster than the bus and more comfortable than the car. Going by bike is better for the environment.)
steps: Learn transport vocabulary including en + vehicle and a pie
Master comparatives: más/menos ... que, mejor/peor que
Practise giving and understanding directions
Learn prepositions of place for describing locations

method_card.title: Weather and Holiday Activities
method_card.content:
Key Vocabulary

SpanishEnglish
Hace solIt's sunny
Hace calorIt's hot
Hace fríoIt's cold
Hace buen tiempoThe weather is good
LlueveIt's raining
NievaIt's snowing
Está nubladoIt's cloudy
tomar el solto sunbathe
nadar en el marto swim in the sea
hacer turismoto do sightseeing
ir de comprasto go shopping
comprar recuerdosto buy souvenirs
descansarto rest

Grammar Focus — Past Continuous

The past continuous describes what was happening: estar in the imperfect + gerund (-ando for -ar verbs, -iendo for -er/-ir verbs). Example: Estaba nadando (I was swimming). Combine with the preterite for scene-setting: Estaba tomando el sol cuando empezó a llover (I was sunbathing when it started to rain).

Model Paragraph

"El verano pasado fui de vacaciones a la playa. Hacía sol y el agua estaba clara. Cada mañana nadábamos en el mar y por la tarde tomábamos el sol. Estaba descansando cuando empezó a llover."
(Last summer I went on holiday to the beach. It was sunny and the water was clear. Every morning we swam in the sea and in the afternoon we sunbathed. I was resting when it started to rain.)
steps: Learn weather expressions using hace, llueve, nieva, hay, and está
Master holiday activity vocabulary in present and past tenses
Practise the past continuous (estaba + -ando/-iendo) for scene-setting
Combine preterite, imperfect, and past continuous in a paragraph

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Hacía sol y nadé en el mar.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Hacía sol = It was sunny (imperfect — weather description).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Nadé = I swam (preterite — completed action). En el mar = in the sea.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: It was sunny and I swam in the sea.

worked_examples.question: Form the past continuous: 'Yo _____ (nadar) cuando empezó a llover.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Past continuous = estar in imperfect + gerund. Yo estaba + gerund of nadar.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Nadar is an -ar verb → gerund is nadando.

steps.label: Answer

wrong.hace: hace is the present tense. The time phrase ayer (yesterday) requires a past tense.
wrong.hará: hará is the future tense (it will be). Ayer is past, not future.

wrong.nado: nado is the present tense. Ayer requires the preterite.
wrong.nadaba: nadaba is the imperfect — used for habitual past actions, not a single event yesterday.

Grammar Focus — Four Tenses

Show range by using four tenses: Present (Uso mi móvil cada día), Preterite (Ayer mandé mensajes), Imperfect (Antes no tenía móvil), Future (En el futuro usaré la tecnología para trabajar). The perfect tense (haber + past participle) adds further range: He comprado un portátil nuevo (I have bought a new laptop).

Model Paragraph

"Uso mi móvil cada día para mandar mensajes y buscar información. Por un lado, es útil porque puedes mantenerte en contacto con amigos. Por otro lado, paso demasiado tiempo en las redes sociales."
(I use my phone every day to send messages and search for information. On one hand, it is useful because you can keep in touch with friends. On the other hand, I spend too much time on social media.)

method_card.title: My House and Home
method_card.content:
Key Vocabulary

SpanishEnglish
la cocinathe kitchen
el salónthe living room
el dormitoriothe bedroom
el cuarto de bañothe bathroom
el jardínthe garden
una camaa bed
un armarioa wardrobe
un escritorioa desk
encima deon top of
debajo deunder
al lado denext to
haythere is / there are
mi casa tienemy house has

Grammar Focus — Hay, Tiene, and Prepositions

Use hay (there is/are) to describe what is in a room: En mi dormitorio hay una cama. Use tiene (has) for what your house has: Mi casa tiene un jardín. Prepositions of place describe position: encima de (on top of), debajo de (under), al lado de (next to). For the past: había (there was/were) and tenía (had). For ideal home: conditional — tendría (would have), habría (there would be).

Model Paragraph

"Mi casa tiene tres dormitorios, un salón grande y un jardín pequeño. En mi dormitorio hay una cama cómoda al lado de la ventana y un escritorio encima del cual hay una lámpara. Mi casa ideal tendría una piscina enorme."
(My house has three bedrooms, a big living room, and a small garden. In my bedroom there is a comfortable bed next to the window and a desk on top of which there is a lamp. My ideal house would have a huge pool.)
steps: Learn rooms of the house and furniture vocabulary
Master hay and tiene for describing your home
Practise prepositions of place to say where things are
Use the conditional to describe your ideal home

Key Vocabulary

SpanishEnglish

un puebloa village/town

el parquethe park
el cinethe cinema

el mercadothe market

se puedeyou can / one can

Grammar Focus — Se Puede and Opinions

Use se puede + infinitive to say what you can do: Se puede ir de compras (You can go shopping). Negative: No se puede hacer mucho (You can't do much). Use lo mejor es que / lo peor es que for balanced opinions. Conditional for ideal town: Mi ciudad ideal tendría (My ideal city would have), habría (there would be).

Model Paragraph

"Vivo en un pueblo pequeño. Hay un parque, una biblioteca y muchas tiendas. Lo mejor es que es tranquilo. Lo peor es que no hay cine. Mi ciudad ideal tendría un cine y más restaurantes."
(I live in a small village. There is a park, a library, and many shops. The best thing is that it is quiet. The worst thing is that there is no cinema. My ideal city would have a cinema and more restaurants.)

Master se puede + infinitive for describing activities
Use lo mejor / lo peor for balanced opinions
Describe your ideal town using the conditional

method_card.title: The Environment and Global Issues
method_card.content:
Key Vocabulary

SpanishEnglish
el medio ambientethe environment
la contaminaciónpollution
el cambio climáticoclimate change
el calentamiento globalglobal warming
el reciclajerecycling
la basurarubbish
reciclarto recycle
ahorrar energíato save energy
ahorrar aguato save water
apagar las lucesto turn off the lights
las energías renovablesrenewable energy
proteger el medio ambienteto protect the environment
plantar árbolesto plant trees

Grammar Focus — Obligation and Future

Use se debe + infinitive (one must), deberíamos + infinitive (we should), hay que + infinitive (it is necessary to), and es importante + infinitive (it is important to) for obligations. The future tense is formed by adding endings to the infinitive: -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án. Example: Reciclaré más (I will recycle more). Irregular stems: tener → tendr-, hacer → har-, poder → podr-.

Model Paragraph

"Hago todo lo posible para proteger el medio ambiente. Reciclo, no malgasto agua y voy en bici al instituto. Deberíamos usar menos plástico. En el futuro usaremos energías renovables."
(I do everything possible to protect the environment. I recycle, I don't waste water, and I go to school by bike. We should use less plastic. In the future we will use renewable energy.)
steps: Learn environmental problems and eco-friendly actions vocabulary
Master obligation phrases: se debe, deberíamos, hay que, es importante
Practise the future tense for discussing environmental plans
Use three tenses in a paragraph about the environment

steps.label: Step 1

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Usar is regular → usar + emos = usaremos.

steps.label: Answer
